Adult BMI Calculator

Calculate body mass index (BMI) from your height and weight. BMI is a quick screening measure for adults, and this page explains what it can and cannot show.

Educational estimates only. Results are not medical advice, a diagnosis, or a treatment plan. Talk to a qualified healthcare professional about your health. Read the full medical disclaimer.

Adults only (18–120).

Example: 170

Height

How to use this calculator

  1. Enter your age (18 or older).
  2. Pick metric or imperial units.
  3. Enter your height and weight.
  4. Press Calculate to see your BMI to one decimal place and the adult category.

The formulas

BMI = weight (kg) ÷ [height (m) × height (m)].

Adult BMI categories
BMIAdult screening category
Below 18.5Underweight
18.5–24.9Healthy weight range
25.0–29.9Overweight
30.0 or aboveObesity category

Limitations of BMI

BMI does not measure body fat directly and cannot tell muscle from fat, so very muscular people can have a high BMI without excess fat. It also does not show where fat is carried. Ethnicity, age and health conditions can change what a given BMI means. Do not use adult categories for children or teenagers.

Frequently asked questions

What is a normal BMI?

For adults, a BMI from 18.5 to 24.9 is called the healthy weight range in standard screening categories. It is a population-level guide, not a verdict on one person.

Is BMI accurate for athletes?

Often not. Muscle is dense, so a muscular person may have a high BMI without excess body fat.

Does BMI diagnose a health problem?

No. It is a screening measure only. A healthcare professional looks at many other factors.

Can children use this calculator?

No. Children and teenagers need BMI-for-age percentiles, not adult categories.
